source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies nonparametric sample selection with endogenous treatment and weak selection monotonicity, gives sharp intensive-margin complier treatment-effect bounds, and develops efficient orthogonal/debiased inference.

The article studies probability-of-benefit bounds for ordinal outcomes, including imperfect randomized-study settings with and without no-defiers assumptions; it has no post-treatment selection-defined principal stratum.
The article partially identifies MTEs for always-observed individuals, gives uniformly sharp bounds under increasingly restrictive assumptions, and includes a monotone sample-selection refinement.
The paper defines breakdown frontiers for ATE and proportion-benefiting conclusions under simultaneous relaxations of random assignment and rank invariance, with asymptotic inference.
The article constructs a pointwise-consistent confidence interval for the fraction benefiting in randomized trials with ordinal or binary outcomes.
The article gives calibrated-projection inference for projections of partially identified parameters in moment-(in)equality models.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 42(2), 2024, pp. 563-578
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article obtains uniform inference through randomly perturbed linear-program value functions for linear functionals or scalar subvectors of moment-inequality identified sets.
The work gives output-sensitive polyhedral decomposition for multiparametric LCPs with sufficient matrices, with lexicographic treatment of degeneracy.
The paper introduces lexicographic perturbation for degenerate multiparametric linear programs to obtain a nonoverlapping explicit solution representation.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a strict inclusion theorem with a concrete observed-law witness showing that the minority-budget class strictly contains both named one-sided-selection comparator classes while preserving the ordinal survivor-complier target.

Promote finite-sample coverage to a clearly labeled corollary of projection lifting and make the exact projection/lifting theorem the sole headline kernel; this prevents a routine multinomial inversion consequence from diluting novelty.
Correct the Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen bibliography pagination to Biometrika 111(4), 1429-1436, and retain exact section anchors for every comparator claim.

For a higher-tier route, prove a computable equivalence/non-equivalence frontier against at least two named selected-complier procedures, rather than only positioning the new class as informed by them.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with projection lifting as the field-tier kernel; keep the chart enumerator as an explicitly separate open computational target.
